title: When the Monsoon Burns
premise: Noor Iversen, a disgraced storm chaser drowning in debt to the Kessler brothers, takes a salvage job retrieving abandoned government survey equipment in the Vantaa Range. What he finds instead is a survivor, Ilse Brandt, and evidence the team didn't vanish—they were erased, because their atmospheric data proved the government's weather-modification program was destabilizing the monsoon cycle. Pursued by the program's fixer, Major Adeyemi, and shadowed by his own creditors, Noor must choose between selling the data to clear his debts and carrying it over the pass to expose the truth. Betrayed by the man who hired him and nearly broken by the range itself, Noor reaches the valley town of Solheim as the first snow falls, broadcasting the data at the cost of the compass—his father's last gift—and finally belonging to something larger than himself.
about_author: Wren Oyelaran is a former meteorological field researcher who traded instrument shelters for writing desks after a decade of monsoon seasons across three continents. They live in a coastal town where the weather is famously boring, and write about places where it isn't.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the port city of Karva, Noor loses a chase contract, watches a storm he predicted destroy a client's fleet, and faces the Kessler brothers' deadline. He accepts a salvage job from a smooth stranger named Corven: recover survey gear from the Vantaa Range. Beat: desperation dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Compass and Debt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, flashback-woven. Preparing for the climb, Noor reflects on his father's brass compass and the career-ending forecast he got right and was punished for. He signs Corven's contract without reading the exclusivity clause. Beat: a man selling his last clean thing.

chapters.title: Into the Green Staircase
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The ascent begins through monsoon-soaked foothills. He finds the survey team's base camp intact but wrong—meals half-eaten, instruments still running, and a logbook with pages cut out. Beat: unease sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: No Tracks
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following the team's route, he finds gear scattered where no one would drop it and no footprints in soft ground. At night he spots a light moving on the ridge—too steady for a survivor, too deliberate for a ghost. Beat: the mountain is watching back.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, first appearance. She's been surviving alone for eleven days, hiding from the light on the ridge. She watches the stranger at her old camp and debates whether he's rescue or a hunter. She decides to make contact on her terms. Beat: calculated hope.

chapters.title: The Knife in the Tent
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse takes Noor's pack hostage to force a conversation, then shows him the data drive she pulled from the survey instruments—readings proving the monsoon is being deliberately altered. She names the program: CLEAR SKY. Beat: the salvage becomes a burden.

chapters.title: What Corven Bought
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Decoding Corven's contract, Noor realizes he wasn't hired to recover gear—he was hired to confirm no witnesses remained. The light on the ridge is Adeyemi's patrol, tracking Corven's beacon. Beat: betrayal reframes everything; loyalty to whom?

chapters.title: The River That Runs Backward
chapters.summary: Ilse and Noor, alternating. Fleeing the patrol, they cross a flooded gorge where the modified weather has reversed seasonal flows. Ilse nearly drowns; Noor's storm instincts save her. Beat: trust forged in water, not words.

chapters.title: The Keslers Arrive
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The Kessler brothers' advance man, Dov, catches them at a waystation—Corven sold Noor's route to the debt. Dov offers to forget the debt if Noor hands over the drive. Noor refuses and they flee into the treeline. Beat: the price of the truth is now everything.

chapters.title: Adeyemi
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. The fixer is not a monster; he believes CLEAR SKY prevents famine, and that Ilse's team died of their own recklessness. He closes the valley's passes with an engineered storm, trapping everyone above the snowline. Beat: conviction as the most dangerous weapon.

chapters.title: The Herder's Hut
chapters.summary: Noor and Ilse, alternating. Sheltering with an old herder, Maret, they learn the valleys below have had three failed harvests—weather the locals whisper is 'borrowed.' Maret feeds them and says nothing, asking only that they remember. Beat: belonging offered by a stranger.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The engineered storm hits. They lose the tent, half the food, and the route. Noor's frostbitten hands can barely hold the compass. Ilse realizes the drive's battery is dying—the data has an expiration date. Beat: the mountain collecting its toll.

chapters.title: Dov's Bargain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dov finds them again, half-frozen himself, and switches sides—Adeyemi's storm killed his nephew in the lowlands. He gives them the patrol's rotation but warns: Corven is coming up the mountain himself. Beat: an enemy becomes an ally; loyalty shifts like weather.

chapters.title: Corven's Ascent
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. The broker climbs with mercenaries, telling himself Noor is a line item, not a person. We learn Corven's own debt—to the program's backers—and that he chose Noor precisely because Noor's ruin made him predictable. Beat: the banality of selling people.

chapters.title: The Ice Bridge
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The only route to the pass is a glacier bridge Adeyemi's storm has cracked. Ilse crosses; the bridge fails under Noor; he saves himself by driving his ice axe through his father's compass case, sacrificing the instrument. Beat: the past released to buy the future.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Ilse and Noor, alternating. At the col, Corven's mercenaries corner them. Dov turns on Corven; a fight in the whiteout leaves Dov dead and Corven fleeing. Ilse takes a bullet graze. They have hours, not days. Beat: victory that feels like loss.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Truth
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Confronting them alone at the pass, Adeyemi shows Noor the famine projections CLEAR SKY was built to prevent—then admits the model is failing, the monsoon destabilizing beyond control. He lets them pass, choosing to report the failure himself. Beat: an enemy's loyalty to his own conscience.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The race down the melting-freezing slope with a dying drive and a wounded Ilse on his back. Noor navigates by storm-sense alone, the old knowledge he was exiled for. Beat: the disgraced skill becomes the saving grace.

chapters.title: Solheim
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They reach Solheim as the first true snow falls. The town's single radio mast is guarded by Corven, waiting with the Keslers for his payday. Ilse realizes the drive can broadcast once—there is no second chance. Beat: the last door, and it's guarded.

chapters.title: One Frequency
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax. Noor trades himself to Corven for the mast key, then—using the storm-reading skills that ruined him—times the broadcast to a lightning strike that fries the mast after transmission and blinds Corven's escape. The data goes out on every open frequency. Beat: the truth, paid for in full.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Adeyemi's confession corroborates the data; the program is suspended; Corven and the Keslers scatter under investigation. Noor, cleared of his old disgrace, is offered his career back. Beat: vindication that arrives quieter than expected.

chapters.title: The Empty Case
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Spring. Noor and Ilse visit Maret's valley, where the harvest is honest again. Noor carries the empty compass case, no longer needing it to find his way. He stays—not as a visitor, but as a neighbor. Beat: belonging, finally chosen rather than owed.
